drivingQuestion: Why does the verse invoke the God of Jacob and not the God of Abraham and Isaac?
outcomeNote: The difficulty in the verse's wording is answered by the derived principle; nothing is left standing.

segments.he: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אָבִין הַלֵּוִי: מַאי דִּכְתִיב ״יַעַנְךָ ה׳ בְּיוֹם צָרָה יְשַׂגֶּבְךָ שֵׁם אֱלֹהֵי יַעֲקֹב״, אֱלֹהֵי יַעֲקֹב וְלֹא אֱלֹהֵי אַבְרָהָם וְיִצְחָק? מִכָּאן לְבַעַל הַקּוֹרָה שֶׁיִּכָּנֵס בְּעׇבְיָהּ שֶׁל קוֹרָה.
segments.en: «And Rabbi Avin HaLevi said: What is» the meaning of «that which is written: “The Lord will answer you on the day of distress; the name of the God of Jacob set you upon high”» (Psalms 20:2)? Is God specifically «the God of Jacob and not the God of Abraham and Isaac?» Rather, «from here» the general principle is derived: «One who owns a beam should approach» carrying «the thick portion of the beam.» A builder, carrying a beam in order to affix it in a building, must calibrate it and measure carefully so that the thick part of the beam fits in its place; so too must Jacob, who fathered and raised the children who would become the people of Israel, continue to pray for them and complete the task of nation-building.
